title: 1967 AHSME Problem 29
statement: \(AB\) is a diameter of a circle. Tangents \(AD\) and \(BC\) are drawn so that \(AC\) and \(BD\) intersect in a point on the circle. If \(AD=a\) and \(BC=b,\) \(a\ne b,\) the diameter of the circle is:

solutions.text:
Let \(d=AB\) be the diameter. Since the intersection of \(AC\) and \(BD\) lies on the circle, those two lines are perpendicular by Thales’ theorem. Also the tangents \(AD\) and \(BC\) are parallel. The resulting right triangles \(ADB\) and \(BCA\) are similar, so \[ \frac da=\frac bd. \] Hence \(d^2=ab\) and \(d=\sqrt{ab}.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Let the intersection point on the circle be \(P\); then \(\angle APB=90^\circ\)
Use the parallel tangents to compare right triangles \(ADB\) and \(BCA\)
